newsitem.title: USA: CME plans to re-list Bradys for physical delivery.
newsitem.headline: CME plans to re-list Bradys for physical delivery.

text.p: The Chicago Mercantile Exchange plans on Friday to de-list cash-settled Brady bond futures and options, beginning with the September contract, the exchange said.
In their place, the exchange plans on the same day to list physical delivery Brady bond futures and options contracts, according to a CME special executive report.
The move requires Commodity Futures Trading Commission approval.

Cash-settled futures and options on four Brady bonds -- Argentine FRB, Brazilian C and EI, and Mexican Par bonds -- began in March 1996. Most of these contracts have had little or no open interest. As of Wednesday, open interest was 261 contracts in June Argentine FRB Brady bonds and nil in the others.
June contracts will not be affected by Friday's proposed change and will expire normally at 1030 CDT/1530 GMT on Monday, the CME said.
CME spokeswoman Ellen Resnick said the change was in response to customer input.
"This is something that the end users said that they wanted and it was really in response to customer demand," Resnick said.

In addition to being re-listed for physical delivery, the Mexican Par Brady bond will undergo changes in its technical specifications. Pending approval, contract size will increase to $250,000 from $100,000 and tick value will increase to $25 per 0.01 point, the CME said.
